---
title: "Suppression is a status"
jupyter: coi-docs
---

Surveillance sources hide small or unreliable numbers for good reasons —
protecting privacy in a small population, avoiding an estimate too noisy to
publish. But "hidden" is not the same fact as "missing," and a lot of
downstream harm comes from collapsing the two into one blank cell.

`value_status` is a closed, documented enum on every row of
`measure.observation`:

| `value_status` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `reported` | value published |
| `suppressed_small_count` | below the source's count threshold |
| `suppressed_complementary` | suppressed to prevent back-calculation |
| `suppressed_reliability` | suppressed because the estimate is unreliable |
| `not_available` | source publishes no value for this unit |
| `not_applicable` | combination is meaningless (e.g. cervix × male) |

The invariant: **`value` is `NULL` whenever `value_status` is not
`'reported'`, and never otherwise.** No reader has to parse a sentinel
(`"*"`, `"3 or fewer"`, `-1`) to find out — and no reader can accidentally
average a suppressed cell in as a zero, because there's no number there to
average.

## Verified against the live catalog

```{python}
#| echo: false
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("INSTALL iceberg; LOAD iceberg; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;")
con.execute(
    "ATTACH 'canceronice' AS coi (TYPE ICEBERG, "
    "ENDPOINT 'https://icegate-canceronice.seandavi.workers.dev', "
    "AUTHORIZATION_TYPE 'none');"
)
zero_leaks = con.sql("""
    SELECT count(*) FROM coi.measure.observation
    WHERE value_status != 'reported' AND value IS NOT NULL AND valid_to IS NULL
""").fetchone()[0]
print(f"Rows where value_status != 'reported' but value is not NULL: {zero_leaks}")
```

Real counts by source, as of this render:

```{python}
#| echo: false
con.sql("""
    SELECT source, value_status, count(*) AS n
    FROM coi.measure.observation
    WHERE valid_to IS NULL
    GROUP BY 1, 2
    ORDER BY 1, 2
""").df()
```

Two sources carry almost all of the suppression here. State Cancer
Profiles' cancer counts are frequently small at the county level — its
`suppressed_small_count` share dwarfs every other source's, exactly as
expected for county-level cancer incidence and mortality. PLACES,
model-based and published only above a minimum population threshold, has a
much smaller suppressed slice. `not_available` on AHRF, FARA, RUCC and SVI
is a blank source cell, not a suppression rule — the source simply didn't
publish a value for that unit (see each source's page in
[Sources](/sources.qmd) for its own missing-value convention). `not_applicable`
on RUCA marks a zero-population, no-identifier tract — a real "this
combination doesn't apply" case, not a hidden number.

## What this means for a query

Never filter on `value IS NOT NULL` as a stand-in for "give me the real
data" without also checking what's *behind* the NULLs you dropped — a county
missing from your result because it's `suppressed_small_count` is a
different finding than one missing because the source never covered it at
all (`not_available`). The [suppressed-cells recipe](/recipes/suppressed-cells.qmd)
runs this page's own query live, in your browser.
